q-40841.name: Question 1
q-40841.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of ${q}_{32}\cdot {r}_{12}.$
q-40841.worked_solution:
Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**. We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}\{{v}_{1}\}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-\frac{6}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & 2\sqrt{3} \\ 0 & \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{3} & 2\sqrt{3} \\ 0 & \sqrt{6}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Finally, ${q}_{32}\cdot {r}_{12}=(\frac{1}{\sqrt{6}})\cdot (2\sqrt{3})=\sqrt{2}.$

q-95937.name: Question 3
q-95937.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {q}_{1} & {q}_{2} & {q}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} & {r}_{13} \\ 0 & {r}_{22} & {r}_{23} \\ 0 & 0 & {r}_{33}\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. You're given that the system of equations given below connects the columns of $Q$ and the columns of $A.$  

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{q}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1} \\ {q}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{a}_{2}+{q}_{1} \\ {q}_{3}=\frac{1}{4}{a}_{3}-{q}_{1}+2{q}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

What is the value of ${r}_{11}+{r}_{12}+{r}_{33}?$
q-95937.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite the vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ as a linear combination of the vectors ${q}_{1},{q}_{2},{q}_{3}:$

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{q}_{1}=\frac{1}{3}{a}_{1} \\ {q}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}{a}_{2}+{q}_{1} \\ {q}_{3}=\frac{1}{4}{a}_{3}-{q}_{1}+2{q}_{2}\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}=3{q}_{1} \\ {a}_{2}=-2{q}_{1}+2{q}_{2} \\ {a}_{3}=4{q}_{1}-8{q}_{2}+4{q}_{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, this system can be written in matrix form as follows:

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} & {a}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {q}_{1} & {q}_{2} & {q}_{3} \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{r}_{11}+{r}_{12}+{r}_{33}=3+(-2)+4=5.
$$

q-96026.name: Question 4
q-96026.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ of $A$ are orthogonal, and that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained by normalizing the columns of $A,$ what is the value of ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{12}?$
q-96026.worked_solution:
Since the columns of $A$ are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix $Q,$ we simply normalize ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{a}_{1}}{‖{a}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{‖{a}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{7}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of $A=QR$ by ${Q}^{T},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{6}{7} & \frac{2}{7} & \frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{6}{7} \\ 0 & \frac{2}{7} \\ -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & \frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 7\end{aligned}]}}
$$

Finally, ${q}_{31}\cdot {r}_{12}=-\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\cdot 0=0.$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix A shown above. Given that the columns a1,a2 of A are orthogonal, and that the columns q1,q2 of Q were obtained by normalizing the columns of A, what is the value of q31⋅r12?

EXPLANATION

Since the columns of A are already orthogonal, to construct an orthogonal matrix Q, we simply normalize a1 and a2:

q1=a1‖a1‖=15[10−2]q2=a2‖a2‖=17[623]

Now, pre-multiplying both sides of A=QR by QT, we obtain

R=QTA=[150−25672737][1602−23]=[5007].

[1602−23]⏞A=[1567027−2537]⏞Q[5007]⏞R

Finally, q31⋅r12=−25⋅0=0.

q-96033.name: Question 5
q-96033.problem:
$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{q}_{11} & {q}_{12} \\ {q}_{21} & {q}_{22} \\ {q}_{31} & {q}_{32}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}{r}_{11} & {r}_{12} \\ 0 & {r}_{22}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Consider the QR factorization of the matrix $A$ shown above. Given that the columns ${q}_{1},{q}_{2}$ of $Q$ were obtained from the columns of $A$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, find  the value of ${q}_{12}\cdot {r}_{22}.$
q-96033.worked_solution:
Let ${a}_{1},{a}_{2}$ be the columns of $A.$

First, we find an orthonormal basis of $\text{Col}(A)=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ using the Gram-Schmidt process.

**Step 1**. We set ${v}_{1}={a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

**Step 2**. We find the vector ${v}_{2}$ orthogonal to $\text{Span}\{{v}_{1}\}$ using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-{\text{proj}}_{{v}_{1}}{a}_{2} \\  & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-(-\frac{6}{18})[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ -2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we normalize ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{q}_{1} & =\frac{{v}_{1}}{‖{v}_{1}‖}=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {q}_{2} & =\frac{{v}_{2}}{‖{v}_{2}‖}=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $R:$

$$
\begin{aligned}R & ={Q}^{T}\,A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{2} & -\sqrt{2} \\ 0 & 3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following QR factorization of $A:$

$$
\overset{A}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}]}}=\overset{Q}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}]}}\overset{R}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{2} & -\sqrt{2} \\ 0 & 3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]}}.
$$

Finally, ${q}_{12}\cdot {r}_{22}=(\frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}})\cdot (3\sqrt{2})=4.$
